source_metadata.title: Activation of ferritinophagy is required for the RNA-binding protein ELAVL1/HuR to regulate ferroptosis in hepatic stellate cells
source_metadata.source_type: basic-science translational study combining HSC cell-line experiments, randomized murine BDL fibrosis experiments, and a single-center retrospective human sorafenib cohort

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary and supplemental source material were treated as one packet. Atomization covers the study objective, experimental populations/exposures, key mechanistic methods, independent main and supplemental findings, human translational component, limitations, conclusion, funding, and conflict disclosure. Bibliographic references were not atomized.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether ELAVL1/HuR regulates ferroptosis in hepatic stellate cells and tested whether ELAVL1-dependent autophagy/ferritinophagy contributes to liver-fibrosis modulation.
In vitro experiments used human HSC-LX2 and rat HSC-T6 hepatic stellate-cell lines.

source_anchor.paragraph: Cell culture conditions and drug treatment

population.label: Human HSC-LX2 and rat HSC-T6 hepatic stellate-cell lines

atoms.canonical_statement: Ferroptosis was induced in HSC lines with erastin, buthionine sulfoximine, or sorafenib; ferrostatin-1 and other death-pathway inhibitors were used to test cell-death specificity.

exposures.details: 5–10 µM depending on assay; 24 h

atoms.canonical_statement: Cell viability, GSH, redox-active iron, malondialdehyde/lipid peroxidation, lipid ROS, and multiple live/dead staining assays were used as convergent ferroptosis readouts.

Erastin, BSO, and sorafenib produced ferroptotic phenotypes in HSC-LX2 and HSC-T6 cells, and ferrostatin-1—but not apoptosis or necroptosis inhibitors—reversed the characteristic cell-death and biochemical changes.
Ferroptosis-inducing compounds increased ELAVL1 protein expression without a corresponding increase in ELAVL1 mRNA, consistent with post-transcriptional regulation.

Cycloheximide limited erastin-associated ELAVL1 protein accumulation, MG-132 augmented ELAVL1 protein abundance, and erastin prolonged ELAVL1 protein half-life, supporting reduced proteasomal degradation as a mechanism of ELAVL1 accumulation.
ELAVL1 was experimentally perturbed with siRNA-mediated knockdown and plasmid-mediated overexpression before exposure to erastin or sorafenib.
ELAVL1 knockdown reduced erastin- and sorafenib-associated growth inhibition and ferroptotic biochemical changes, whereas ELAVL1 overexpression intensified them.
Ferrostatin-1 and liproxstatin-1 reversed ferroptotic growth inhibition in ELAVL1-overexpressing HSCs, while apoptosis and necroptosis inhibitors did not, further supporting a ferroptotic mechanism.
ELAVL1 overexpression increased LC3-II conversion, BECN1 expression, autophagic flux, and autophagic vesicles while decreasing SQSTM1/p62; ELAVL1 silencing produced the opposite pattern.
During erastin-associated ferroptosis, HSC-LX2 cells had approximately 8 ± 4 autophagic vesicles/cell with control treatment, 4 ± 2 with ELAVL1 siRNA, and 14 ± 3 with ELAVL1 overexpression.

population.label: HSC-LX2 cells assessed by transmission electron microscopy

exposures.details: Control, ELAVL1 siRNA, or ELAVL1 plasmid before erastin

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean autophagic vesicles per cell in ELAVL1-overexpression group
quantitative_result.original_result_text: Control 8 ± 4 vesicles/cell; ELAVL1 siRNA 4 ± 2; ELAVL1 plasmid 14 ± 3.

atoms.canonical_statement: BECN1 knockdown reduced LC3-II conversion and made HSCs resistant to erastin- and sorafenib-associated ferroptotic phenotypes, including when ELAVL1 was overexpressed.
BECN1 overexpression promoted ferroptotic phenotypes and synergized with ELAVL1 overexpression, supporting BECN1-dependent autophagy as a mediator of ELAVL1-enhanced ferroptosis.
BECN1 knockdown increased FTH1 and prevented ELAVL1 overexpression from substantially reversing that increase, whereas BECN1 overexpression reduced FTH1 and synergized with ELAVL1 overexpression.

The ELAVL1–BECN1 interaction was tested with ribonucleoprotein immunoprecipitation, biotinylated RNA affinity isolation, 3′-UTR fragment mapping, and luciferase reporters containing wild-type or deletion constructs.
ELAVL1 preferentially interacted with the BECN1 mRNA 3′-UTR, especially the F3 region spanning positions 1404–1774 that contains AU-rich elements.
Deleting the BECN1 F3 3′-UTR region abrogated ELAVL1-mediated luciferase upregulation, supporting a functional role for this RNA-binding region in BECN1 mRNA stabilization.
The in vivo experiment used 50 eight-week-old male C57BL/6 mice randomized into five groups of 10 with comparable mean body weight.

population.label: Eight-week-old male C57BL/6 mice randomized to five experimental groups

atoms.canonical_statement: After bile-duct ligation, mice received sorafenib 10 mg/kg intraperitoneally every other day for 2 weeks and/or vitamin-A-coupled liposomal ELAVL1 siRNA 0.75 mg/kg intravenously three times weekly for 2 weeks; control-siRNA and sham groups were included.
Murine liver fibrosis was assessed by macroscopic examination, H&E, Sirius Red, Masson staining, Ishak fibrosis staging, hydroxyproline, and ACTA2/COL1A1 measurements.
Sorafenib reduced histologic and molecular evidence of BDL-induced liver fibrosis, whereas HSC-targeted ELAVL1 knockdown largely abrogated the antifibrotic effect.

In isolated primary mouse cells, sorafenib triggered PTGS2 induction, redox-active iron accumulation, lipid ROS, and lipid peroxidation in HSCs but not in primary hepatocytes or macrophages under the tested conditions.
RNA-seq compared primary HSCs isolated from sorafenib-treated BDL mice receiving VA-Lip-ELAVL1-siRNA versus VA-Lip-Control-siRNA, using >1.4-fold for upregulation and <0.65-fold for downregulation.
In ELAVL1-silenced primary mouse HSCs, 347 mRNAs were upregulated and 421 were downregulated relative to control-siRNA HSCs during sorafenib treatment.
In sorafenib-treated primary mouse HSCs, ELAVL1 silencing was associated with MAP1LC3B/LC3B expression of 0.21-fold relative to the control-siRNA condition.

atoms.canonical_statement: HSC-targeted ELAVL1 knockdown blunted sorafenib-associated autophagy/ferritinophagy signals and reversed ferroptotic readouts in the murine BDL model.
The retrospective human component included 28 patients with advanced liver fibrosis and HCC who received sorafenib monotherapy; 15 were male and 13 female, with mean age 56.8 ± 12.6 years.

atoms.canonical_statement: Sorafenib-treated human HSC samples showed lower expression of fibrosis-associated genes including ACTA2 and COL1A1 and higher autophagy/ferritinophagy and ferroptosis signals, including increased NCOA4, ELAVL1, PTGS2, iron, ROS, and lipid peroxidation.
Supplementary Figure S1 showed erastin-associated HSC death by trypan blue, FDA, and calcein-AM/PI assays and selective reversal by ferrostatin-1 rather than apoptosis or necroptosis inhibitors.
Supplementary Figure S2 showed GSH depletion and iron accumulation after erastin, BSO, or sorafenib, with ferrostatin-1 reversing these ferroptotic events.
Supplementary Figure S3 supported ELAVL1-dependent autophagy by showing changes in autophagy-related transcripts, long-lived protein degradation, and chloroquine-sensitive LC3-II accumulation.
Supplementary Figure S5 showed that HSC-targeted ELAVL1 knockdown opposed sorafenib-associated reductions in fibrosis markers and altered ferroptotic readouts in the murine model.

Cell and animal experiments were performed in duplicate or triplicate and repeated three times with matched controls; analyses used Student t tests or one-way ANOVA with Student-Newman-Keuls testing, while the human retrospective analyses used chi-square/Fisher exact tests and paired t or Wilcoxon tests as appropriate with p<0.05.

RNA-seq reads were aligned with TopHat and differential expression analyzed with edgeR; adjusted p values used the Benjamini-Hochberg method, with >1.4-fold and <0.65-fold thresholds for up- and downregulation.
The human study obtained written informed consent and institutional review approval and stated conformity with the Declaration of Helsinki.
The mouse procedures were approved by institutional/local animal-care committees and were stated to follow NIH animal-care guidance.
The authors identified inherent selection bias from the retrospective human sample selection.
The authors noted that the number of patients with liver-biopsy tissue available for mechanistic analysis was small.
The human component was single-center, and the authors stated that this limited generalizability and required multicenter confirmation.

The authors concluded that ELAVL1 binding to BECN1 mRNA is a key event linking autophagy activation, ferritin degradation, and HSC ferroptosis, and proposed this pathway as a potential basis for antifibrotic diagnostic or therapeutic development.
The authors reported no potential conflict of interest.
The work reported support from multiple National Natural Science Foundation of China awards and Jiangsu institutional/provincial programs.
